Scenario Quick Start

Quick path

Use this checklist when you want the shortest safe editing path.

Public starter samples

Download original JSON
  1. 1. Apply Scenario Apply a scenario first so ownership, controller, support tools, and project surfaces share the same baseline.
  2. 2. Select the target country in Inspector Open the right-side Inspector and confirm that the selected country is the one you actually want to edit.
  3. 3. Confirm HGO identity when needed When the selected country comes from HGO data, review its HGO names, flag option, and ideology label before changing ownership.
  4. 4. Set the active owner Political actions read the current Active Owner. Check the Active chip in the top bar before you commit any change.
  5. 5. Edit, style, then save Use Activate or Scenario Actions for map edits, tune Appearance and Transport for readability, then save a project JSON before export.

Before you edit

Before editing, look at the chips at the top of the map. Mode shows the active tool, View shows the map state you are seeing, and Split shows how many countries have split ownership. If any chip looks wrong, switch to the correct scenario or project first.

Before a large edit or before loading another project, save a backup: open Project Management and download the current project JSON. Loading a project replaces the current map, notes, and export settings.

After loading a project, check the Inspector again. Confirm the target country and active owner, then review frontlines, reference image alignment, and export settings. When these match your plan, continue with Activate, Scenario Actions, or Export.

HGO and identity

Use this section when the scenario uses HGO source data, HGO flags, or HGO country-name variants.

HGO runtime preview Check the donor geography before editing.

HGO preview helps you inspect the HGO source layer beside the active scenario map. It is best used before ownership, label, or color decisions.

  • Use whenYou need to compare the active map against HGO geography or confirm that the selected feature belongs to the expected source region.
  • OrderApply the HGO-backed scenario, open the preview, select the target country, then read the Inspector before changing anything.
  • CheckThe selected country, owner tag, and visible boundary should describe the same place before you edit.
HGO identity Review names, flags, and ideology variants.

The Inspector can show HGO names, flag options, and ideology labels for the selected country. Treat these as identity choices for display and review.

  • Use whenA country needs a specific HGO display name, flag variant, or ideology label before export.
  • OrderSelect the country, enable the HGO identity view in Inspector, pick the intended identity option, then review the map label and flag preview.
  • CheckThe visible name, flag option, ideology label, and active owner should match your scenario notes.

Appearance and transport

Use Appearance for map readability and Transport for routes, ports, airports, and network context.

Appearance panel Tune the visual language of the main map.

Appearance covers borders, ocean, rivers, city points, physical regions, day-night lighting, textures, and presets. These controls change how the same scenario reads on screen and in export.

  • Use whenThe map needs clearer borders, softer terrain, visible cities, stronger coastlines, or a reusable visual style.
  • OrderSet base borders and water first, add physical or day-night layers, then adjust labels, textures, and presets.
  • CheckZoom out and zoom in once; borders, cities, water, and terrain should stay readable at both scales.
Transport panel Control visible transport context on the main map.

Transport controls the overview layer for airports, ports, rail, and roads. The visual mode changes whether you read distribution, network shape, or coverage.

  • Use whenYou need routes, hubs, ports, airports, or infrastructure density visible beside political ownership.
  • OrderTurn on Show Transport Overview, choose Distribution, Network, or Coverage, then tune each family visibility, labels, and scope.
  • CheckOpen Transport Workbench when you need pack preview, layer order, diagnostics, data rows, or apply-to-map controls.

Editing tools

Use these tools for ownership edits, batch changes, annotations, and source-aligned visual work.

Inspector and active owner Pick the target and the owner before painting.

The Inspector tells you what country or feature is selected. The Active Owner tells paint and ownership actions which country receives the edit.

  • Use whenYou are about to change ownership, controller, cores, labels, or any feature-level state.
  • OrderSelect the map feature, read Inspector, set Active Owner, then use Activate, Fill, Eraser, or Scenario Actions.
  • CheckThe top chips and Inspector should agree on mode, selected target, active owner, and split status.
Batch and annotation tools Use broad edits and strategic marks deliberately.

Scenario Actions, Quick Fill, special zones, frontlines, operational graphics, and unit counters help you move from single-country edits to a readable campaign map.

  • Use whenOne click should affect a group, a region, a frontline, or a planned operation.
  • OrderMake a project save, choose the exact scope, run the batch action, then inspect several affected countries.
  • CheckAfter a broad edit, review View, Split, labels, frontlines, and export preview before the next broad action.

Publishable map tools

Use Project tools as a publish checklist: save the project, add strategic context, align references, then export.

Project Management Save and restore the complete working state.

Contains Download Project, Load Project, selected file status, and import safety checks.

  • Use whenYou are about to make broad ownership, frontline, transport, or overlay changes.
  • OrderDownload a project JSON first, load another file only after confirming the current state can be replaced, then re-check the top status chips.
  • CheckAfter import, confirm scenario baseline, current owner, strategic annotations, and export settings before continuing.
Frontlines & Annotations Build the publishable strategic layer.

Contains derived frontlines, operational lines, operation graphics, and unit counters. These are project-local strategic annotations for export and handoff.

  • Use whenThe political map needs readable conflict edges, arrows, planned operations, or visible unit counts.
  • OrderTurn on derived frontlines first, then add operational lines and graphics, then place counters near the final composition.
  • CheckBefore export, make sure Strategic annotations are enabled and no line, label, or counter hides the country you want to show.
Reference Image Align an external map or sketch.

Contains local image upload, opacity, scale, horizontal offset, and vertical offset controls. The project stores alignment values, while the image file must be uploaded again after reload.

  • Use whenYou need to trace historical borders, compare a source map, or keep a visual planning layer beside the scenario.
  • OrderUpload the image, set opacity for readability, adjust scale, then fine-tune horizontal and vertical offsets.
  • CheckHide or lower the reference before final export unless you intentionally want it visible in the composition.
Export Preview layers, resolution, and final output.

Contains target selection, format, export resolution, preview, layer order, text stacks, and image adjustments. Final export is capped at 8K.

  • Use whenThe map is ready for a composite image, per-layer PNG set, or bake pack handoff.
  • OrderChoose target and resolution, check the preview, confirm layer order, then run the export.
  • CheckKeep Strategic annotations enabled when frontlines, operational graphics, or unit counters must appear in the final output.

Success checks

Treat saving and exporting as two separate handoff steps: save the editable project first, then export the publishable image or layer package.

Project JSON save The editable handoff file.

Use Download Project to save the current editable state: scenario choice, ownership edits, appearance, transport, strategic annotations, reference alignment values, and export settings.

  • Use whenYou need a recovery point, a handoff file, or a before-and-after checkpoint before a broad edit.
  • OrderDownload the JSON, reload it once with Load Project, then confirm the same scenario, annotations, labels, and export settings return.
  • CheckThe image file used by Reference Image is not embedded; upload it again after loading, then verify the stored alignment values still fit.
Export workflow The publishable output step.

Use Open workbench to choose the output target, format, resolution, layer order, text stacks, and image adjustments. Export creates the final image, per-layer PNG set, or bake pack; it does not replace the editable project JSON.

  • Use whenThe map is ready for publishing, screenshot handoff, layered editing, or bake-pack delivery.
  • OrderPick the target, set resolution, inspect preview, confirm layer order and strategic annotation visibility, then run export.
  • CheckComposite image is for final viewing; per-layer PNG is for later editing; bake pack is for a bundled delivery with expected layers.
Final handoff check The last pass before sending files out.

Before sending files out, keep one editable project JSON and one exported output from the same reviewed state. This keeps later fixes traceable.

  • Use whenYou are preparing a final image, sharing the scenario with another editor, or archiving a stable milestone.
  • OrderReview labels, borders, strategic annotations, reference visibility, and export target before the final click.
  • CheckIf the exported result looks wrong, reopen the saved project JSON, fix the editable state, then export again from that corrected state.
